chapter.learnedFrom: Genki I, Genki II, and So-Matome N3 Kanji Week 1, Day 1 – Week 3, Day 1

sentences.japanese: 設定料金に労務費用は含みません。
sentences.english: The stated price does not include labor charges.

sentences.japanese: 諸設備の費用は払っていただきます。
sentences.english: You have to pay for utilities.

tokens.g: to pay (e.g. money, bill); to brush off

sentences.japanese: 医者の費用は本当に貯金に食い込む。
sentences.english: Doctors' bills really cut into our savings.

tokens.g: to bite into (e.g. rope into skin)

words.gloss: consumer (of a product, service, etc.); customer; (end) user

sentences.japanese: 多くの消費者は消費税反対に立ち上がった。
sentences.english: Many consumers rose up against the consumption tax.

tokens.g: to stand up; to get up

sentences.japanese: 消費者の米離れや国際市場解放が原因とされる米価の下落が原因だ。
sentences.english: It is the drop in the rice pricing (blamed on consumers' loss of interest in rice and the freeing up of the international market) that is the cause.

sentences.japanese: 日本からの輸入製品がアメリカの消費者市場に浸透するには長い時間がかかった。
sentences.english: It took a long time for Japanese imports to penetrate the American consumer markets.

sentences.japanese: 春休みはどれくらいの期間ですか。
sentences.english: How long is your spring vacation?

sentences.japanese: 貸借の期間が短ければ交友期間は長い。
sentences.english: Short accounts make long friends.

sentences.japanese: 治るのにどのくらいの期間がかかりますか。
sentences.english: How long will it take to get well?

tokens.g: to get better; to get well

sentences.japanese: 長期予報によると、暖冬だそうだ。
sentences.english: The long-range forecast says we will have a mild winter.

sentences.japanese: それは大成功で長期興行になった。
sentences.english: It was a great success, ending in a long run.

tokens.g: that is in; who is called

sentences.japanese: 長期にわたる病気のあとでジェーンはカウチ・ポテトになった。
sentences.english: After being ill for a long time, Jane turned into a couch potato.

tokens.g: illness (usu. excluding minor ailments, e.g. common cold)
that is in; who is called

words.gloss: to restrict; to limit; to confine

sentences.japanese: 大男が必ずしも頑強だとは限らない。
sentences.english: A big man is not always robust.

sentences.japanese: 金持ちが必ずしも幸福とは限らない。
sentences.english: The rich are not always happy.

sentences.japanese: 料理のレパートリーは限られてるの。
sentences.english: I don't know how to cook too many things.

sentences.japanese: この製品はイタリア製だ。
sentences.english: This product is made in Italy.

sentences.japanese: この製品は飛ぶように売れています。
sentences.english: These products are selling like hot cakes.

tokens.g: to sell (well); to be well known

sentences.japanese: 原油は精製されて多くの製品を産出する。
sentences.english: When refined, crude oil yields many products.

words.gloss: best-before date (on food); use-by date; expiry date

sentences.japanese: このパンって賞味期限大丈夫か？
sentences.english: Is this bread's best-by OK?

sentences.japanese: 今年の冬は気温が平均以上だ。
sentences.english: The temperature is above average this winter.

sentences.japanese: 気温が下がると関節が痛むんだ。
sentences.english: My joints ache when it gets cold.

tokens.g: to come down; to go down

sentences.japanese: 今朝は気温が氷点下に下がっている。
sentences.english: The temperature has fallen below zero this morning.

tokens.g: to come down; to go down

sentences.japanese: 日増しに暖かくなっている。
sentences.english: It's getting warmer day by day.

sentences.japanese: 青い麦畑には暖かい陽光が満ちている。
sentences.english: The warm sunlight is full upon the green wheat field.
